about: One entry per ticket. The Kanban on the canvas (page Kanban) and the handover read this file. States: later (one line, an idea), next (brainstormed, Milan's answer in, no board), now (board drawn and approved, waits for Go), progress (branch open), done (merged, with its version). Milan says the word; Claude moves the card. From 18 November 2026 a ticket can carry five parts: opportunity (why we act on it: where it comes from, the job the person was doing, what stood in the way as one of the kinds below, and why now), problem (the pain today, in plain words), story (what the person wants to be able to do and why, never the solution), ac (the acceptance criteria for what is new only: scenarios with an id, a short title that names the behaviour, and one sentence Given ..., when ..., then ...; one behaviour each), and unchanged (what already works and must not change: preconditions, not requirements). Kinds of what stood in the way: could not do it, a bug; could not do it, the feature is missing; too many steps; did not find it or did not understand it; a risk of a wrong tap; looks broken. The opportunity says honestly who saw it: a tester in a test, or Coach Milan's own look. Decided 18 November 2026, 12:41, for every ticket from the next one on (DT311 is the example): the Kanban card is short and names the ticket's board as a text label (no link); the board carries the weight. On the board, a vertical card holds the request (opportunity, problem, story) and then the solution and the decision; the screens are the design; a wide block at the bottom holds the agreement: the acceptance criteria as a table (#, Scenario, Given, When, Then), what already works and must not change, and design details for the build. A board is named by its ticket id, never by its file name. The full description is the Project note claude/chef-mealan-ticket-form.md and docs/ticket-form.md. A ticket can also carry findings (what was checked, with the date) and open (the open questions); both show on its board.

details: Too light: a weight under the WHO underweight line for the height (BMI under 18.5). The EU uses the same lines: Eurostat's BMI classes and the European Commission's Knowledge for Policy gateway follow WHO (18.5, 25, 30), independent of age and sex. The app calculates it and never shows a BMI number.

Too much body fat: over the top of the healthy range by sex and age, from Gallagher et al. 2000 (Am J Clin Nutr 72:694), which links body fat to the WHO BMI lines. Women 33 % (20 to 39), 34 % (40 to 59), 36 % (60 to 79); men 20 %, 22 %, 25 %. There is no EU or WHO line for body fat itself; EASO's 2024 framework adds a waist-to-height ratio, which the app does not ask for.
Target range: a gain up to the top of the healthy weight for the height (BMI 25); a loss down to the underweight line (BMI 18.5), no top limit, so a muscular man is not stopped.
Pace: gain roughly 1 kg a month (Coach Milan 16:12); loss 0.5 to 1 % of the body weight a week, as the Lose fat card already says.
